title: Preprocessor directives
hook: C# “preprocessor” directives are compiler switches, not a separate C preprocessor. `#nullable` is a project-level safety switch whose behavior lives in the null-safety module.

sections.heading: #if, #region, #pragma, #nullable
sections.prose: `#define TRACE` at the top of a file (or `DefineConstants` in the csproj) gates `#if TRACE` / `#elif` / `#else` / `#endif`. Use this for diagnostic-only logging in a RabbitMQ publisher, not for swapping entire implementations — that belongs in DI. `#region` / `#endregion` are editor folding; they mean nothing at run time. `#pragma warning disable CSXXXX` should be scoped and justified. `#error` and `#warning` emit diagnostics (`#error version` prints language version). `#line` rewrites diagnostic line numbers (generators). `#nullable enable|disable|restore` (and `enable warnings`) toggles nullable reference type analysis for the following code. Treat `#nullable` as a switch: it does not change CLR representation of `string` versus `string?` for references; the annotations and warnings are explained in module 07. File-based `#:` directives are SDK config, not this set.

snippets.label: Conditional compile versus nullable switch
snippets.explanation: #if strips code from the compilation. #nullable only changes static analysis. Do not mix them in your head.

interviewTakeaways: `#if` removes tokens before bind; it is not an `if` statement.
`#nullable` is an analyzer/compiler switch; full NRT rules are module 07.
commonPitfalls: Shipping a `#if DEBUG` security bypass that is off in Release — still a design smell.
Disabling nullable at file scope to silence warnings instead of fixing types.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS has no `#if`. Bundlers drop unused modules; C# `#if` drops tokens before compile. TS `/// <reference>` is a different kind of directive.
